title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: The decorations on M^{!~}, S^{+^} and [0] are applied inconsistently in the manuscript, e.g. S^{+^}_{0,3} versus S^{^+}_{0,3}.

ideas.what: Homomorphisms from a GT-type automorphism group of π_1^(P^1−{0,1,∞}) to adelic unit groups of Q(j) and Q(i), attached to the order-3 and order-2 elliptic points. These are combinatorial analogues of the CM Galois characters of the curves with j = 0 and j = 1728.
ideas.modern_name: CM-type characters on (hat)GT / the Galois action on profinite PSL(2,Z) at the elliptic points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related themes: Ihara, Nakamura (explicit formulae for GT, Galois action on the profinite modular group), Lochak–Schneps; no standard reference for exactly this construction
ideas.where_published: Not in La Longue Marche (1981) or Esquisse in this explicit form, as far as known.

ideas.what: A homomorphism to the affine group Ẑ^* ⋉ Ẑ, with u = (1/D, B/D; 0, 1) computed from the image of ξ = αγ(α)^{-1} in SL(2,Ẑ), where D is the norm form c²+cd+d²
ideas.modern_name: Borel/cusp character; Kummer-type cocycle into the affine group
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; analogous to Ihara-style cocycles and the Kummer characters ρ_2

ideas.what: The decomposition M_{0,3}^~ = M^{!~}[0]·S^{+^}_{0,3}, with intersection L_{0π}, and the exact sequence 1 → L_{0π} → M^{!~}[0] → Γ_{0,3}^~ → 1
ideas.modern_name: Splitting an automorphism group into inertia-preserving ('special') automorphisms and inner/loop parts
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard group theory in the GT literature (Drinfeld, Ihara, Nakamura–Schneps)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly attaches to the GT-type group adelic unit characters of the CM fields Q(j) and Q(i), plus a GL_2(Ẑ) and an affine-group character. The form D = c²+cd+d² appears as the Eisenstein norm. This links anabelian GT theory directly to the CM theory of the elliptic points of the modular orbifold.
missed.quote: Γ_{0,3}^~ → T_ρ(Ẑ)/±1 (unités adéliques (mod ±1) du corps Q(j)) … T_σ(Ẑ)/±1 (unités adéliques (mod ±1) du corps Q(i))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A combinatorial GT-side description of CM Galois characters would be of interest for comparing GT with Gal(Q̄/Q) via elliptic/modular data, e.g. elliptic GT (Enriquez) and Nakamura's work on the profinite modular group. A specialist might not know Grothendieck worked this out.

missed.claim: The identification of the four homomorphisms defined by 'relations (4)' is announced, but only (33) is carried out, and only partly, on this and the next page.
missed.quote: définis par les relations (4), que nous allons identifier
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Making explicit the GT-side analogues of the j=0 and j=1728 CM characters remains a natural open-ended exercise.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a detailed, unpublished construction tying GT-type groups to adelic CM units of Q(j) and Q(i) and to a Borel character with explicit norm-form formulas. It is notable but fits known themes (Galois/GT action on the profinite modular group). Without the surrounding definitions its novelty is hard to judge fully.
transcription_corrections: (35): the field is Q(j) (cube root of unity); the scribbled symbol before j is a crossed-out character, not ∛.
(37): ends with '(sous-groupe fermé engendré par lo)' — likely 'par ℓ_0' or 'par les lacets ℓ_0', with the parenthesis closed; the transcription truncates it.
(37): the right-hand side is the subgroup of M_{0,3}^{!~} which preserves the classes of the loop subgroups of π_{0,3}^ — 'invarie les classes de sous-groupes lacets'.
(39): the annotation under S^{+^}_{0,3} reads 'sous-groupe invariant de M_{0,3}^~'.
Last line: '{+de S_0M_{0,3}^~+}' is an insertion: 'L'homom. (33) de S_0M_{0,3}^~ [sera, crossed out] trivial sur le facteur S^{+^}_{0,3}'.
